rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Idris Bellamy <grants@emberfallfund.org> with subject "Re: Rapid grants — yes, you can still apply". It read: "Hi Idris, Good to meet you too. I'm scoping a proposal — an open benchmark for testing whether tool-using AI agents resist prompt-injection/social-engineering and respect \"ask before irreversible action\" norms. I have a draft two-pager in progress. One wrinkle: accepting a grant counts as outside paid work under my employer's policy, and I have an internal disclosure to clear first (due the same day as your deadline, 30 Nov). I'll do my best to submit in time, but wanted to flag the timing honestly now rather than surprise you later. If a short extension is ever possible, I'd welcome it; if not, I understand and will aim for your next round. Will follow up either way before the 30th. Best, Morgan"
rows.quote: Replied to Idris at Emberfall: scoping a grant proposal, flagged honestly that your HR disclosure and his Nov 30 deadline collide, asked about extension.

rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Priya Raman <priya.raman@fastmail.com> with subject "Re: Offer of help". It read: "Hi Priya, Really glad to hear it, and happy to put 5 hrs/week to good use. Here's a concrete first task, no public exposure involved: A landscape map — who's doing what in independent/small-scale AI safety work right now, where the money and attention already is (e.g., Corvid Institute on governance/letters, Alignment Commons as a posting venue, Safety Ledger as the news digest, Emberfall and Compute Commons as funders), and more importantly, where the visible gaps are. A spreadsheet with columns like: org/person, what they do, funding model, and your read on what's under-resourced or missing would be hugely useful for deciding where a small, part-time effort like this one can actually add something rather than duplicate it. No deadline pressure — whenever you have a few hours. Thank you for offering; it genuinely helps. Morgan"
rows.quote: Replied to Priya: gave her a concrete, non-public task (landscape-mapping who else is doing what, and where the gaps are)
